Subject: Pilot ask: BlueNova wants MFN + exclusivity for discounted pilot — need exec decision

Team —

Quick summary: BlueNova (prospect) is asking for a 6-month paid pilot at 55% off list with two high-risk commercial asks: a 12-month MFN (most-favored-nation) clause covering pricing for the product family, and a limited exclusivity restricting their target vertical (clinical search assistants) while pilot is live. They sent a redline (attached) and SOC2. Deal ID BN-2029-042.

Why this is high risk: MFN locks unit economics across verticals for 12 months (hard to unwind if we change packaging), exclusivity could block competitor pilots in an important mid-market segment, and the discount is substantially below our standard pilot pricing.

What I propose we escalate with options for the execs:
- Option A (conservative): Decline MFN, offer a time-bound, pilot-limited exclusivity (30 days post-pilot) and a 25% pilot discount.
- Option B (conditional): Approve a 6–12 month MFN but narrow scope to the initial SKU set and require performance milestones + min ARR commitment; exclusivity limited to pilot scope only.
- Option C (approve full ask): 55% discount + 12-month MFN + pilot exclusivity — requires explicit exec signoff and SLA deviations.

Attachments: BlueNova_Redline_Termsheet_v3.pdf, SOC2-attestation.pdf, pricing_analysis.xlsx.

Asks: 1) Can the execs sign off on any of these options (A/B/C)? 2) If not, what is the maximum discount or additional commercial guardrail we should require?

Timeline: BlueNova wants to sign and kick off week of Apr 8. I need a directional decision by EOD Thu so legal can prepare redlines.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Courtney —

Thanks for the redline and the timeline. We want to move quickly but need to document a few guardrails before committing MFN/exclusivity externally. Internally I am escalating this to execs today with details and options. To help expedite, here are the constraints Redwood would need to accept any MFN/exclusivity: 

1) Scope limit: MFN must be limited to the identical SKU set used in the pilot (no automatically binding future bundles or enterprise-only SKUs).
2) Performance gates: MFN becomes active only if BlueNova meets the agreed conversion and usage milestones during the pilot (we will outline milestones in an appendix).
3) Timebox: Any exclusivity must be strictly timeboxed to pilot duration + 60 days post-pilot and scoped only to the mid-market clinical search use-case; global enterprise sales excluded.
4) Min revenue: A minimum second-year ARR commitment (or a mutual good-faith review) to trigger extended protections.
5) Pricing exceptions: Redwood must retain the right to offer promotional pricing publicly provided we include a carve-out where we must offer BlueNova the same terms if they request matching within 30 days (this is the MFN carve-out).

If BlueNova accepts these constraints we can present Option B to execs for conditional approval. If not, we will propose Option A (no MFN, limited exclusivity, 25% discount) as our default.

We will aim to get a directional exec decision by Thu EOD. Please confirm if BlueNova can accept the performance-gated MFN construct.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Subject: Escalation to Execs: BlueNova BN-2029-042 — recommendation and decision matrix

Leadership —

I am elevating this thread for executive signoff. Summary of key tradeoffs:
- Commercial ask: 55% pilot discount + 12-month MFN + pilot-limited exclusivity.
- Legal risk: Broad MFN without narrow SKU scope materially limits our ability to reprice or repackage; exclusivity restricts go-to-market in a vertical we consider strategically important.
- Operational: SLA concessions have been requested in the redline (response windows and uptime credits) — these need explicit approval.

Recommendation: Present execs with three clear choices (A/B/C). My legal team recommends Option B only if we get: explicit SKU-scoped MFN, milestone gating, a minimum renewal ARR commitment, and a 30-day MFN-match window (not automatic for promotional pricing).

Decision matrix for execs (choose one):
A) Decline MFN, offer 25% pilot discount, pilot-only exclusivity (30 days post-pilot), no SLA exceptions. (Low risk)
B) Approve conditional MFN: 12 months but SKU-scoped, activated by meeting milestone thresholds and subject to a min ARR commitment; approve pilot exclusivity limited to mid-market clinical search for pilot + 60 days; authorize up to 35% discount. (Medium risk; requires legal to sign final language)
C) Approve full customer ask: 55% discount + 12-month broad MFN + exclusivity as redlined; requires Executive signature and explicit SLA deviations. (High risk)

Please reply-all with A, B, or C and any additional constraints. If B or C are chosen, legal will finalize language and finance will prepare the concession memo for finance approval.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
